SYMPTOM: Startup migration was mangling valid ISO timestamps like `2025-07-28T18:56:27Z` — matching `28T18:` and replacing `T18:` with `:18:`.
CAUSE: Regex `(\d{2})T(\d{2}:)` was written to match malformed `18T56:` but also matches the valid `28T18:` in the date→time boundary. The two-digit sequence before `T` exists in both valid and malformed forms.
FIX: Changed to `(T\d{2})T(\d{2}:)` — requires the full time-section `T` before the malformed `T`. This uniquely matches `T18T56:` → `T18:56:` without touching valid `28T18:`.
NEW TESTS CAUGHT THIS — the 8 migration tests in `platform_services::tests` failed on valid ISO timestamps before the fix. This is why real tests > fake mock tests.
PREVENT: Always test timestamp regex against both valid AND malformed examples in the same test.
